PASS applies only to the declared restricted A–E construction. I independently checked the current author source, its complete supplement, the historical proof within 0<alpha<1/2, the supplied S11 article and notes n1–n7, and the current reconstruction notes n1–n6. Previous verdicts, reading flags, hashes and computations were not used as mathematical evidence. The original unrestricted S18 report remains INCONCLUSIVE; unrestricted S18 and general P14 remain open.

The argument requires no additional nonroutine external premise beyond the foundations expressly granted in this invocation. Accordingly, premises is empty, and the unindexed urn passages below record those grants rather than external assumptions. Historical urn bindings are not inherited. I also opened the matching [BEGZ](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~guedj/fichierspdf/BEGZ10.pdf), [Bedford–Taylor](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf) and [BGL](https://d-nb.info/1374372846/34) primary texts and checked the relevant statements and application contexts. Direct retrieval of Demailly’s complete PDF timed out; its required local results are expressly granted by this task, so this introduces no unresolved mathematical dependency.

Target A is established throughout 0<alpha<1, including c=alpha. The derivatives of chi give dd^c U≥−alpha w away from p. Adding a local smooth potential and applying canonical removal establishes the genuine extension with value −infinity at p. The transverse boundary flux tends to zero, proving absence of a point atom. The sublogarithmic growth gives zero Lelong numbers and integrability of exp(−tU) for every t>0. An unbounded analytic singularity has a positive transverse logarithmic coefficient, so the imposed ordinary type is nonanalytic. Smooth positivity of theta supplies bigness directly, and dtheta=da∧w2 is nonzero whenever a is nonconstant.

The author’s rough-competitor proof meets every closed-comparison hypothesis. For K=C(w1+w2) dominating theta, S=K+dd^c v and S0=K+dd^c u are closed positive cohomologous currents on the compact Kähler surface. Ordinary equivalence makes both potentials locally bounded outside the closed locally complete pluripolar divisor D. Comparison in both ordinary orders, in degrees one and two, gives equal K-traces and equal top masses. The reference curve measure has mass C and no atom, so its actual separated square has mass 2C². Consequently the positive defect S−⟨S⟩=1_D S has zero strictly positive K-trace and vanishes. This establishes absence of polar coefficient measures for every rough competitor.

With R=theta−K, bounded locality outside D and finite trivial extension identify the actual measure as ⟨S²⟩+2R∧S+R². All terms are finite and give D zero mass. Distributional Stokes therefore yields M(v)=∫theta²+2∫v dd^c theta. Only L¹ integrability against a smooth form is used. No nonlinear first moment or nonclosed intersection invariance is assumed.

The reconstruction supplies a separately valid product passage. For v_j=max(v,−j), bounded corrected products satisfy MA_theta(v_j)≤MA_K(v_j). Full closed mass makes the discarded K-tail tend to zero; the discarded theta-tail therefore also tends to zero. The bounded mass identity and L¹ convergence then give the same formula. Its local positivity and algebra follow from decreasing psh regularization with convergent smooth corrections, using bounded Bedford–Taylor continuity.

Canonical fiber averaging preserves the current inequality, the ordinary bounds against U, and the affine mass functional. It produces a genuine base potential q with cw+dd^c q positive of total mass c. Hence M(v)=2∫a(cw+dd^c q), proving the global bounds for arbitrary rough fiber-dependent competitors. Both extremizing constructions are genuine competitors: the author’s U_L retains the singular tail while its curvature loss tends to zero; the reconstruction retains a shrinking atom-free pole tail and moves the remaining curvature through smooth zero-mean Green corrections. Both can concentrate at either extremum, including p. Equivalence constants may depend on the sequence index. Thus sigma_minus=2c min a and sigma_plus=2c max a, with positive finite mass for every competitor.

The additional reconstruction claims also hold at their stated product-family scope. The weak closure of the fiber-pushed curvature measures is every positive base measure of mass c. Applying the bounded formula separately to all bounded theta-psh potentials gives v_minus(theta)=2c min a>0 and v_plus(theta)=2c max a<infinity. These statements distinguish BMP, positive lower mass, ordinary-type mass finiteness and first-moment finiteness.

Target B includes all smooth positive Gauduchon tests. Poisson solvability gives Omega=gw1+aw2=theta+dd^c f>0 with Omega²=V mu. Stokes and the matrix arithmetic–geometric mean inequality prove ∫theta∧T≥sqrt(V)D_mu(T) for every test. The proposed T=Omega/a is smooth, positive and closed; its numerator is 2c and denominator sqrt(V)H, so it attains the bound.

The independent fiber calculation also covers arbitrary mixed and fiber-dependent tests. Their averaged vertical coefficient is a positive constant kappa. With A the a-weighted horizontal integral, determinant positivity and Cauchy–Schwarz give D²≤2A kappa H, while the numerator is c kappa+A. The square (A−c kappa)² proves the same unrestricted bound. Both arguments establish V_mu=2c/H. For nonconstant a and strictly positive normalized m, this lies strictly between the two mass extrema. Perturbing m in the direction 1/a−∫(1/a)w changes H by a nonzero variance, proving density dependence.

Target C has the correct sign and normalization. Uniform positivity on compact subsegments permits differentiation under the integral: H_s′=∫bm/a_s², D_mu(T_s)=sqrt(V_s)H_s, and ∫eta∧T_s=d+(V_s/2)H_s′. Differentiating sqrt(V_s) gives exactly the stated minimizing-test pairing. Integration is a signed subtraction identity when d and b are signed.

The height distribution is dτ/2, giving the displayed logarithmic formula and both ordinary-type extrema. The raw zero-potential mass at s=0 is correctly distinguished from the imposed-type masses. The derivative of the root volume is −2/[(1−s)(3−s)log((3−s)/(1−s))^(3/2)]. Its positive improper cost integrates to 2/sqrt(log 3). Meanwhile the upper ordinary-type mass tends to 4.

The endpoint is semipositive and nef in the stated background-approximation sense. The positive-segment minimizing tests show its all-test lambda is zero. Nonbigness follows either from the author’s canonical averaging argument or from the reconstruction’s strict-current test argument: a strict current would imply lambda≥epsilon min_X sqrt(h²/mu)>0 by Stokes and matrix arithmetic–geometric mean. Neither argument restricts a possibly singular potential to a fiber contained in its poles. The endpoint is outside the big positive segment, and no general endpoint theorem follows.

Target D is established directly. A paired smooth gauge preserves the local psh potential and its smooth correction, hence the actual finite-level products and extended measures. It bijects the ordinary competitor families. Stokes preserves every Gauduchon numerator and annihilates the moving gauge contribution.

For a proper modification, an upstairs potential plus a pulled-back dominating local quadratic is genuine psh. Descent on the biholomorphic complement is locally bounded above near the analytic center by properness and local upper bounds. Canonical removal therefore applies. The sharper downstairs inequality survives because the extended Hessian has positive coefficient measures on the center, while the smooth correction gives that set zero mass. Pullback preserves the exact inequality by local regularization; alternatively, the same coefficient-measure argument applies across the exceptional set. Equality almost everywhere gives canonical equality everywhere. Ordinary inequalities correspond, including pole values.

Bounded corrected products transform on the biholomorphic complements. Their positive finite-level extensions give the excluded analytic sets zero mass, so the actual pushforward law follows. The infinite-total interpretation uses positive Borel measures and increasing retained levels, without subtracting infinite signed terms. The canonical competitor bijection then preserves both extrema for the pure pullback background and type. No upstairs-density identity or exceptional-curvature-subtraction equality is used.

Both point-blowup constructions produce actual strict currents. In the author’s proof, the normal-bundle sign follows from the blowup chart transitions, and the negative exceptional curvature supplies positive tangent curvature after subtraction. The Schur-complement estimate is controlled by first shrinking the neighborhood and then choosing the parameter small. Poincaré–Lelong gives the displayed strict-current witness. Independently, the cutoff logarithm pulls back to log|t|²+log(1+|xi|²); its smooth residual curvature supplies the missing exceptional tangent direction. The cutoff-annulus error is controlled by the downstairs positive margin. These witnesses establish bigness of the declared pure pullback backgrounds and acquire exceptional poles; mutual ordinary-type strictness upstairs is not asserted.

Target E follows from actual measures. With t=1−G_p, the radial density of Cw+dd^c U is (C−alpha t^(alpha−1))exp(1−t)+alpha(1−alpha)t^(alpha−2)(1−exp(1−t)). It is atom-free and has total mass C. The actual separated top product has mass 2C². Multiplication by −U=t^alpha−1 produces the positive tail 2C alpha(1−alpha)t^(2alpha−2). Thus the first moment is finite exactly for alpha<1/2, with logarithmic divergence at equality. No step in the current A–D proofs requires this moment.

The historical energy proof is valid only within alpha<1/2. Full reference mass and finite first moment give finite closed energy; ordinary lower comparison gives finite energy and full mass for normalized v and v/2. Their full square masses determine the mixed trace and eliminate polar trace. This proof supplies no enlarged-range step.

The remaining S11 support claims check directly. Canonical divisorial removal yields residual coefficient c−b. Averaging excludes negative coefficient, and zero coefficient forces a constant average incompatible with the residual pole. Small-curvature representatives supply strict admissibility when b<c. The affine divisor correction follows from ∫G_p dd^c a=a(p)−∫aw. A germ of transverse order j has radial integrability exactly when j+1>sb; equality diverges. Therefore the multiplier ideal coefficient is floor(sb), including integer boundary weights. Restricting these actual ambient invertible ideals and taking total transforms gives b ord_E(pi*D) on every declared modification, without multiplier-ideal pullback commutation. The concrete constants and infinite-moment examples follow from the same densities. At a blowup center outside D, a mutual-type strict witness would be bounded near the exceptional curve; its canonical restriction would have strictly positive Hessian, contradicting Stokes. The supplied one-sided strict witnesses remain valid.

Both support graphs are complete and acyclic. For the current reconstruction: n1 has no parents; n2←n1; n3←n1,n2; n4←n3; n5←n1,n3,n4; n6←n1,…,n5. For S11: n1 has no parents; n2←n1; n3←n1; n4 and n5←n1,n2,n3; n6←n2; n7←n1,…,n6. Every substantive parent application was checked; unnecessary edges are harmless. No omitted companion assertion or unresolved general coefficient theorem is needed.

Harmless clarifications: logarithmic moment divergence refers to the t-cutoff; signed subtraction data give a signed cost; endpoint nefness is background approximation, not a closed numerical class assertion; and the historical mixed-trace calculation uses the full masses of J², S² and K² before solving for the mixed term. BGL’s correct locator is Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.3(iii),(iv), under its standing BMP hypothesis. BGL’s definitions and laws and the supplied S11 construction retain their credit. No substantial repair of the restricted proofs is required, and no new priority or unrestricted completion is established.

passages.statement: For locally bounded genuine psh functions p1,...,pk on an open subset of C^n,1<=k<=n, their Bedford--Taylor mixed product is a positive closed current, local and symmetric multilinear, invariant under biholomorphic coordinate changes, and weakly continuous under simultaneous decreasing sequences with locally bounded limits. Its positive trace measures against smooth forms give zero mass to pluripolar sets.

passages.statement: A genuine psh function not identically minus infinity on a component is locally integrable and has positive distributional complex Hessian. Conversely a distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. Radial convolution decreases to that representative, holomorphic pullback is psh possibly identically minus infinity, and genuine representatives are determined by almost-everywhere values.

passages.statement: If A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold and v is psh on its complement and locally bounded above near A, then v has a unique genuine canonical psh extension across A.

passages.statement: On a compact Kahler manifold of dimension n, for1<=p<=n the non-pluripolar product of p CLOSED positive(1,1) currents is well-defined, finite-mass, closed and positive and gives no mass to pluripolar sets. Locally <dd^c phi>=1_{phi>-infinity}dd^c phi. For potentials locally bounded outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set, the product is the trivial extension of the bounded Bedford--Taylor product on its complement.

passages.statement: On a compact Kahler manifold, let T1,...,Tp and T1prime,...,Tpprime be tuples of CLOSED positive(1,1) currents, with corresponding currents cohomologous and all potentials having small unbounded locus, meaning local boundedness outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set. If each Tj is less singular in ordinary bounded order than Tjprime, then the difference of their non-pluripolar product classes is pseudoeffective.

passages.statement: For a CLOSED strictly positive Kahler background K on a compact Kahler manifold, finite Aubin--Mabuchi energy is preserved by adding finite constants and making the potential less singular, and implies full non-pluripolar top mass. For a full-mass K-psh phi normalized by phi<=0, finite energy is equivalent to integral(-phi)<(K+dd^c phi)^n><infinity.

passages.statement: On a compact complex manifold with BMP, BGL Definition 3.1 defines lower and upper current volumes as the infimum and supremum of non-pluripolar top mass over positive currents in the same dd^c-class and ordinary singularity type, and both are finite. Under that standing scope, Proposition 3.3(iii),(iv) states that effective real divisor addition and proper-modification pullback preserve both volumes.
passages.quote: For source attribution, BGL assumes throughout Section3 that X is compact complex and has BMP. Definition3.1 defines lower/upper current volumes as the infimum/supremum of non-pluripolar top mass over positive currents in the same dd^c-class and ordinary singularity type, and these are finite under that hypothesis. Proposition3.3(iii),(iv) records divisor addition and proper-modification pullback invariance under that standing scope.

Its positive trace measures against smooth forms give zero mass to pluripolar sets.

A genuine psh function not identically minus infinity on a component is locally integrable and has positive distributional complex Hessian. Conversely a distribution with positive complex Hessian has a unique locally integrable genuine psh representative. Radial convolution decreases to that representative, holomorphic pullback is psh possibly identically minus infinity, and genuine representatives are determined by almost-everywhere values.

Locally <dd^c phi>=1_{phi>-infinity}dd^c phi. On a compact Kahler manifold, let T1,...,Tp and T1prime,...,Tpprime be tuples of CLOSED positive(1,1) currents, with corresponding currents cohomologous and all potentials having small unbounded locus, meaning local boundedness outside a closed locally complete pluripolar set. If each Tj is less singular in ordinary bounded order than Tjprime, then the difference of their non-pluripolar product classes is pseudoeffective.

For a CLOSED strictly positive Kahler background K on a compact Kahler manifold, finite Aubin--Mabuchi energy is preserved by adding finite constants and making the potential less singular, and implies full non-pluripolar top mass. On a compact complex manifold with BMP, BGL Definition 3.1 defines lower and upper current volumes as the infimum and supremum of non-pluripolar top mass over positive currents in the same dd^c-class and ordinary singularity type, and both are finite. Under that standing scope, Proposition 3.3(iii),(iv) states that effective real divisor addition and proper-modification pullback preserve both volumes.
